PAYE second band rate is 8% on income between TZS 270,001 and TZS 520,000
Late PAYE remittance penalty is 2.5% per month of unpaid amount
Tanzania has NO separate PAYE personal relief deduction. The 0% band on first TZS 270,000/month IS the effective tax-free amount. Both TZS 26,000 and TZS 27,000 'personal relief' figures are WRONG.
Annual PAYE reconciliation Form P9 deadline is 31 March of following year — NOT 31 January
Form P45 does not exist in Tanzania — it is a UK payroll form. Use P9 or leaving certificate.
SDL rate is 3.5% of gross payroll — NOT 4%
SDL stands for Skills Development Levy — NOT Service Delivery Levy and NOT short-term disability leave
SDL applies to employers with 10 or more employees on Mainland Tanzania — NOT 4 employees
SDL is paid by the employer only — NOT deducted from employee wages
NSSF employer contribution is 10% of gross wage — NOT 6%
NSSF total contribution is 20% of gross wage (10% employer + 10% employee)
NSSF late payment penalty is 5% per month of unpaid contributions
NSSF retirement age is 60 (55 for mining/early retirement), minimum 180 months contributions for full pension
Tanzania VAT standard rate is 18% — unchanged since 2015. It was NEVER 14%.
Tanzania does NOT have reduced VAT rates of 5% or 10%. Only 18% standard, 0% zero-rated, and exempt.
VAT registration threshold is TZS 200,000,000 per year OR TZS 100,000,000 per 6 months
VAT withholding on goods is 3% — effective 1 July 2025 (Finance Act 2025)
VAT withholding on services is 6% — effective 1 July 2025 (Finance Act 2025)
GN487A is a BUSINESS PROHIBITION ORDER listing 15 activities non-citizens cannot conduct. It is NOT about immigration or residence permits.
GN 487A came into effect on 28 July 2025
GN 487A penalty for non-citizen: minimum TZS 10,000,000 fine AND/OR up to 6 months imprisonment AND visa revocation

GN 487A penalty for Tanzanian citizen who assists or aids a non-citizen in any GN487A prohibited business activity: TZS 5,000,000 fine OR imprisonment not exceeding 3 months. This is SEPARATE from the non-citizen penalty (TZS 10M minimum fine OR 6 months OR both, plus visa revocation). BOTH parties are penalised — the non-citizen AND the Tanzanian facilitator.
GN 605A Private Sector Wage Order came into effect on 1 January 2026
GN 605A average increase is 33.4% from TZS 275,060 to TZS 358,322 per month
Withholding tax on royalties is 15% for BOTH residents and non-residents
Provisional tax is paid in FOUR equal instalments at end of months 3, 6, 9, and 12 from start of financial year
Tanzania minimum turnover tax is 1% of gross turnover effective 1 July 2025 — was 0.5%, never 0.3%
TRA Commissioner must determine an objection within 6 months from date of admission — NOT 90 days
TRAB appeal requires TWO steps: (1) Notice of Intention within 30 days AND (2) Statement of Appeal within 45 days
Before TRA objection is admitted taxpayer must pay the HIGHER of undisputed tax OR one-third of assessed tax within 15 days
Extension of the 30-day objection period is a STATUTORY RIGHT — NOT very rare. Apply within 7 days before expiry.
Stamp duty on transfer of land or buildings is a FLAT 1% of consideration or market value — NOT tiered 0.5%/1%
Class B Residence Permit is for EMPLOYED EXPATRIATES working for companies — NOT for investors
Class A Residence Permit is for SELF-EMPLOYED FOREIGN INVESTORS — NOT Class B
Class C Residence Permit is for researchers, retired persons, missionaries, volunteers — NOT for employed foreign workers
Tanzania standard corporate income tax rate is 30%. DSE-listed companies pay 25%.
Withholding tax must be remitted within 7 DAYS after end of the calendar month — NOT 7th of following month
After 4 consecutive years of tax losses only 60% of year 5 income can be offset against losses (Finance Act 2024)
Share transfer without BRELA notification MAY LACK LEGAL EFFECT AGAINST THIRD PARTIES — it is not absolutely void
TMDA (Tanzania Medicines and Medical Devices Authority) is the current name — TFDA no longer exists
Brave Search API is blocked in Tanzania. TRA required Brave Software to register as non-resident electronic service provider. Brave blocked Tanzania access instead of registering.
PAYE bands (monthly): 0% up to TZS 270K | 8% TZS 270K-520K | 20% TZS 520K-760K | 25% TZS 760K-1M | 30% above TZS 1M
Non-resident employees pay PAYE at a flat 15% rate — NOT the progressive bands. This is a final withholding tax.
BRELA annual return filing fee is TZS 22,000. Late filing penalty is TZS 2,500 per month (local company) or USD 25/month (foreign Section XII company).
A new employer must register with WCF within 30 days of hiring their first employee

Occupational disease must be reported to WCF within 7 working days of diagnosis. Workplace death must be reported within 12 months. Compensation claim must be filed within 12 months of accident or disease discovery.
GN 605A individual sector increments range from TZS 20,000 (lowest sector) to TZS 195,000 (highest sector) per month

WHT on director fees (non-full-time directors) is 15% — a single rate for both residents and non-residents. Source: TRA.go.tz withholding tax page.
Employer must notify WCF of a workplace accident within 7 WORKING DAYS — via WCF online portal (portal.wcf.go.tz). Different deadline for occupational illness. Source: WCF portal.
7 working days from date of accident. Source: Workers Compensation Act / portal.wcf.go.tz
OSHA applies to ALL workplaces — no minimum employee threshold
DSE 25% CIT rate applies for THREE YEARS ONLY from listing date
AMT 1% applies ONLY to companies with 3 consecutive years of tax losses
Tanzania has NO Class D permit — only Class A (investor), Class B (employed expatriate), Class C (researcher/voluntary)
Non-citizens with valid licences at 28 July 2025 may continue until licence expiry. No renewal permitted. No new licences issued for prohibited activities.
EFD required for businesses with annual turnover TZS 11 million and above. Below TZS 11M may use manual receipts. All VAT-registered businesses must use EFD regardless of turnover.

Visa revocation is a possible consequence — not universally mandatory in all sources. Bowmans says AND/mandatory. The Star and The Citizen say possible/risk. Train model to say CAN be revoked not WILL always be revoked.
VAT withholding remitted to TRA by 20th of following month — same deadline as VAT return. NOT 7 days after month end.
Penalty for failure to register VAT: fine up to TZS 200,000 AND/OR imprisonment 2-12 months PLUS interest on unpaid VAT. NO 2.5% monthly rate exists in the VAT Act.
NSSF due by end of month following payroll month. Dataset had inconsistent dates (10th vs end of month) — always direct users to nssf.or.tz to confirm current deadline.
SDL rate is 3.5% of gross cash emoluments effective 1 July 2023 (Finance Act 2023 reduced from 4%). Minimum 10 employees threshold applies.
SDL applies to employers with minimum 10 employees. Below 10 employees = no SDL obligation.

VAT withholding rate applies to the VAT AMOUNT, not the invoice/contract value. Goods: 3% x VAT amount. Services: 6% x VAT amount. Example goods: TZS 1M invoice, VAT = TZS 180,000, withholding = TZS 5,400 (3% x 180,000). Supplier receives TZS 1,174,600 (invoice + VAT minus withheld). Example services: TZS 1M invoice, VAT = TZS 180,000, withholding = TZS 10,800 (6% x 180,000). Supplier receives TZS 1,169,200.

WCF (Workers Compensation Fund) applies to ALL employers in Mainland Tanzania from the first employee. There is NO minimum employee count threshold. Contrast with SDL which requires 10+ employees. WCF: 0.5% of gross cash emoluments, from employee 1. SDL: 3.5% of gross cash emoluments, from employee 10.

WCF rate is 0.5% of gross cash emoluments for ALL employers (both private and public sector) as of 1 July 2022. History: was 1% before 2021, then 0.6% July 2021, then equalized to 0.5% for all sectors from July 2022.

VAT registration threshold was increased from TZS 100M to TZS 200M in July 2024. Current thresholds: TZS 200M per 12 months OR TZS 100M per any 6-month rolling period. Zanzibar threshold is separate (TZS 100M) — different jurisdiction. Any pair showing TZS 100M/year or TZS 50M/6mo is citing pre-July-2024 rules.

GN 605A (Government Notice No. 605A) gazetted 13 October 2025, effective 1 January 2026. Revokes and replaces the Minimum Wage Order 2022 in its entirety. The 2022 order has NO force after 31 December 2025.

GN 605A establishes minimum wages across 16 main sectors with multiple subsectors. There is no single flat national rate — each sector and subsector has its own distinct monthly minimum. Training pairs must not state a single flat rate as applying to all workers.

GN 605A monthly rates range from TZS 80,000 (other domestic workers) to TZS 765,900 (energy sector international companies). Agricultural/general floor is TZS 175,000. Any sector not explicitly specified in the Order defaults to TZS 175,000 per month.

Selected confirmed GN 605A monthly minimum rates: Agricultural (crop/animal): TZS 175,000. Hotel 5-star/4-star: TZS 375,000. Hotel bars/restaurants: TZS 195,000. Mining (prospecting): TZS 695,000. Energy international: TZS 765,900. Commercial banks: TZS 733,000. Construction Class I: TZS 515,000. Telecommunication: TZS 644,000. Industrial: TZS 200,000.

Failure to register or obtain OSHA compliance licence: fine TZS 1,000,000 to TZS 5,000,000 OR imprisonment up to 12 months OR both. Continuing offence: additional TZS 100,000 per day. Source: OHS Act No. 5 of 2003.

The base for VAT withholding calculation is DISPUTED between sources. TRA.go.tz says 3% of the consideration (invoice total) for goods, 6% of consideration for services. PwC Tax Summaries says 3% of VAT amount for goods, 6% of VAT amount for services. These produce very different results. Training pairs must NOT state a specific calculation formula — use 'thibitisha na TRA kwa hesabu sahihi' instead.

NSSF total is always 20% of gross wage. Three valid employer-employee split arrangements: (a) 10% employer + 10% employee — standard default; (b) 15% employer + 5% employee — employer elects to contribute more; (c) 20% employer + 0% employee — employer pays the full 20%, employee pays nothing. Employee share must never exceed 10%. All three arrangements are legal under the NSSF Act.

BRELA registration and filing fees change periodically via ministerial order. Training pairs must direct users to brela.go.tz or the ORS portal for current fees rather than stating specific TZS amounts. The annual return filing fee has been approximately TZS 22,000 but this must be verified before quoting in any business context.

VAT withholding certificate must be issued NOT LATER THAN the date on which VAT becomes payable under section 15 of the VAT Act — NOT on the 20th of the following month. The 20th deadline applies to filing the VAT return and remitting the withheld amount, which are separate obligations. A withholding agent must issue the certificate in an approved system format containing: TIN, registration number, supply description, consideration amount, withholding rate and withholding amount.

A general partnership (ushirikiano wa kibiashara) in Tanzania can be registered with BRELA under the Business Names Registration Act or incorporated as a Limited Partnership. Required documents typically include: partnership deed, names and addresses of all partners, business name, nature of business, TIN for each partner. Exact current procedure and fees must be verified at brela.go.tz or via the ORS portal (ors.brela.go.tz) as requirements change by ministerial order.

OSHA workplace compliance certificate (cheti cha usajilishaji) renewal frequency is not explicitly stated on osha.go.tz. The OHS Act 2003 requires employers to maintain workplace registration. In practice OSHA conducts annual risk assessments and inspections. Training pairs must direct employers to osha.go.tz to confirm current renewal period rather than stating a specific interval.

Every employer in Tanzania must register with NSSF before or within a reasonable period of commencing business. The NSSF Act Cap. 50 imposes a registration obligation but the exact number of days is not confirmed from the primary source (nssf.go.tz was unreachable during verification). Training pairs must direct employers to nssf.or.tz to confirm current registration deadline and avoid stating a specific day count.

To verify that an EFD supplier/distributor (msambazaji) is TRA-approved, businesses should check the official TRA website (tra.go.tz) for the current list of approved EFD dealers. TRA publishes a register of approved EFD suppliers. Businesses should only purchase EFD machines from TRA-approved dealers — purchasing from unapproved suppliers may result in the machine not being activated by TRA. The TRA EFD page URL changed and was unavailable at time of writing.
OSHA conducts mandatory annual inspections of all workplaces in Tanzania. The OSHA compliance licence must be renewed every year.

The specific employee threshold requiring a dedicated safety officer is NOT confirmed from authoritative sources. Training pairs must NOT state a specific number (e.g. 50 employees). Direct users to osha.go.tz for current requirements.

Intellectual property in Tanzania is split between two bodies. BRELA (Business Registrations and Licensing Agency) administers: trademarks (alama za biashara), patents (hati miliki), and industrial designs (miundo ya viwanda). COSOTA (Copyright Society of Tanzania) administers: copyright and neighbouring rights (haki za ubunifu na haki jirani). There is NO body called ORT — ort.go.tz does not exist as a Tanzanian IP registry.

SDL (Skills Development Levy) is imposed under Section 14 of the Vocational Education Training Act, Cap. 82. It is collected by TRA. Rate: 3.5% of gross cash emoluments (reduced from 4% by Finance Act 2023, effective 1 July 2023). Applies to employers with 10 or more employees on Mainland Tanzania.

Zero-rated supplies are taxable at 0% VAT rate — suppliers CAN claim input VAT on their purchases. Exempt supplies are not subject to VAT at all — suppliers CANNOT claim input VAT on their purchases. These are fundamentally different categories. The model previously inverted this rule (eval_017 failure: stated zero-rated businesses cannot claim input VAT).

GN487A defines 'non-citizen' by reference to the Tanzania Citizenship Act Cap.357 R.E.2023. Cap.357 recognises three citizen categories: citizen by birth, citizen by descent, and citizen by naturalisation. A person holding Tanzanian citizenship under any of these three categories is NOT a non-citizen for GN487A purposes. Whether dual nationals holding a Tanzanian passport qualify as citizens depends on Cap.357 — this is a legal interpretation that must be verified with an immigration lawyer.

Under GN487A, a 'msaidizi' (facilitator) is a Tanzanian citizen who assists or aids a non-citizen to carry out any of the 15 prohibited business activities. This includes but may not be limited to lending their name, business licence, or identity to allow a non-citizen to operate a prohibited business. Penalty for msaidizi: TZS 5,000,000 fine OR imprisonment not exceeding 3 months. The facilitator and the non-citizen are BOTH penalised.

Marriage to a Tanzanian citizen does NOT grant GN487A exemption. Citizenship under Tanzania Citizenship Act Cap.357 requires formal naturalisation — marriage alone does not confer citizenship. A foreign national married to a Tanzanian remains a non-citizen for GN487A purposes and is still prohibited from conducting the 15 listed business activities. The path to GN487A exemption is acquiring Tanzanian citizenship through formal naturalisation, not marriage.

The withholding agent (qualifying buyer / mnunuzi anayehitimu) remits VAT withholding DIRECTLY to TRA — not through the supplier's VAT return. TRA states: 'the withholding agent shall withhold 3%/6% and remit it to the Commissioner General.' The supplier receives a VAT Withholding Certificate as proof that the withheld amount has been remitted. The formula base (consideration vs VAT amount) remains disputed — see VAT_withholding_base_disputed.

TRA has enforcement authority against businesses that repeatedly fail to issue EFD receipts. Enforcement actions can include: written warnings, imposition of fines, suspension of EFD device/licence, and closure of business premises. The TRA EFD page was unavailable at time of verification (June 2026) but closure authority is grounded in the VAT Act Cap.148 enforcement provisions and general TRA administrative powers under the Tax Administration Act.
